question: When several AI models share one task, how do we make sure nothing important is lost between them?
reflection: Good handovers matter for machines as much as for people, and learning to pass knowledge cleanly helps every team work better.

sources.subject: KV cache techniques for faster, cheaper multi-model AI agents

one_line: Researchers are finding ways for AI models to hand work to each other by sharing their internal memory instead of rewriting everything as text.

top_stories.title: Faster handovers between AI models
top_stories.what: NVIDIA researchers reportedly convert one model's internal working memory so a larger model can continue a task without rereading everything, cutting handover time by up to 25 times on long inputs, with some accuracy trade-off.
top_stories.why: Cheaper handovers make it practical to use a small model for routine coding of data and a larger one only for hard cases.

top_stories.title: Models that pass notes without words
top_stories.what: A separate method lets one model inject what it understood directly into another model's memory, reportedly improving accuracy by a few points and speeding up handovers about 2.5 times compared with text messages.
top_stories.why: These methods need open models you run yourself, another reason to keep self-hosted options in view for sensitive work.

idea.title: Small and large model routing pilot
idea.pitch: Route easy text classification to a small local model and send only unclear cases to a larger one, then measure cost and accuracy.
idea.first_step: Label 300 open-ended survey answers by hand to use as a benchmark.

idea_kids.title: Pass the message relay
idea_kids.pitch: Teams pass a drawing description down a line using words only, then try again with a sketch, and compare how much detail survives.
idea_kids.first_step: Choose three simple pictures and set a time limit for each round.

terms.definition: The working memory a model builds while reading input, so it does not have to reread everything for each new word.
Sending each request to the cheapest model that can handle it well.

concepts.summary: Cheaper handovers between small and large models in one agent system.
Reusing internal memory to avoid repeated computation on long inputs.
